title: Trace viewport: slim mode proposal & interaction notes
content:
Purpose
-----
This is a working sketch for a ‘slim mode’ / viewport-first trace inspector. Goal: reduce vertical real-estate, improve scannability for long traces, and make keyboard/navigation-first workflows smooth for SREs and engineers who are hunting latency regressions across many spans.

Why now
-------
- Customers signal: large traces (hundreds+ spans) are painful to navigate in console; many use local tooling to flatten or filter before uploading.
- Current waterfall rendering is heavy — full DOM for every span, leading to slow scroll on dense traces and high memory.
- Opportunity: give a fast, filter-first inspector that prioritizes visible lanes and progressively renders surrounding context.

Principles
----------
- Viewport-driven rendering: only render spans that intersect a viewport window plus small buffer.
- Compact representation: collapse span rows into a compact “slim” row by default (one line per span) with optional expanded details inline or in a side rail.
- Deterministic keyboard navigation: up/down moves between visible spans (with lazy-fetch of collapsed children), left/right jumps by time buckets (50ms/200ms heuristics).
- Preserve fidelity: compact mode must still allow inspection of exact timing, tags, and logs without leaving the trace view.

Proposed UI elements (wireframe notes)
-----------------------------------
1) Slim viewport (center pane)
- Single-column list of spans left-aligned with micro-metadata: name, service tag, duration (human-readable).
- Right side: condensed waterfall canvas (SVG) scaled to trace duration. Each span is a thin horizontal bar (2–4px height) with color by service. Hover reveals micro-tooltip.
- Visual affordance for collapsed child spans: thin stacked ticks inside parent bar. Clicking bar expands inline.

2) Sticky context rail (right edge)
- When a span is focused, the rail shows: full name, start/end timestamps, top 3 tags, last 5 logs, and quick actions (copy span id, open flame, open raw JSON).
- Rail is keyboard-focusable (tab or `i` to toggle).

3) Mini time navigator (top of viewport)
- A small horizontal scrubber with a clickable viewport window. Dragging the mini-window pans the main scroll. Zoom-in controls (x1/x4/fit).
- Left/right keyboard (or `h`/`l`) moves the mini-window by 10% of total duration.

4) Filter bar (collapsible, top)
- Quick filters: service, status (error/warn/ok), duration (buckets), tag-search (free text).
- Saved filter presets with one-click apply. Show count badge next to filter (approx matching spans visible).

5) Quick-compare lanes (bottom dock, optional)
- Allow up to 3 pinned spans or requests to be shown stacked for side-by-side micro-comparison (useful for regression triage).

Interaction flows
----------------
A. Scan + inspect a large trace (200+ spans)
- User opens trace in slim mode by default for traces > 100 spans.
- Viewport loads top 40 spans plus buffer. Mini navigator shows 5% window.
- User presses `j` / `k` to move focus down/up; focused span gets highlighted and details appear in the right rail.
- To expand children inline, press `space` or `Enter`. Children are inserted but only for the focused parent (prevents reflow).

B. Find slow service occurrences
- In filter bar, type service:name -> dynamic filter applied with counts.
- Results highlighted; user uses `f` to jump to next matching span.
- Matching spans show a small ‘needle’ icon on the waterfall.

C. Time-slice compare
- User selects a short window on the mini navigator and clicks ‘snapshot’. The UI creates a pinned compare lane at bottom that shows aggregates (p95, p99, median) for selected spans/services.

Implementation notes (engineering constraints)
-------------------------------------------
- Use virtualized list (react-window or similar) but with an SVG canvas overlay for waterfall bars to avoid thousands of DOM elements.
- Progressive hydration: initial render paints bars with approximated widths from server-provided start/duration; full metadata fetched on demand for focused spans.
- Keyboard focus model: maintain a flat index array of visible spans; when children are expanded their indices are inserted; update ARIA attributes for accessibility.
- Cache: span detail fetch should be cached per-trace to avoid re-fetch thrash when users tab through spans.

Backlog items (rough grooming)
----------------------------
- TR-4123: Slim viewport baseline prototype (virtualized list + svg bars) — 5 pts (Ravi)
- TR-4124: Sticky detail rail and keyboard model — 3 pts (Maya)
- TR-4125: Mini navigator + snapshot compare lane — 5 pts (Lena)
- TR-4126: Filter grammar + presets UI — 3 pts (Product)
- TR-4127: Accessibility pass (keyboard + screen reader) — 2 pts (SRE/QA)
- TR-4128: Performance benchmark harness (1000-span traces) — 3 pts (Infra)
- TR-4129: UX polish + micro-interactions — 2 pts (Design)

Open questions / trade-offs
-------------------------
- Default mode: should slim-mode be on by default for large traces, or behind a feature flag? Proposal: default on for >100 spans, toggle available in header.
- Inline expansion UX: inserting children inline will shift indices; consider maintaining a sticky focused row to avoid losing context.
- Exact width estimation vs server-side: server can return timeline buckets to avoid client computing absolute pixel widths — reduces layout thrash but increases payload size.
- Heatmap vs precise bars: for very dense traces a heatmap overlay may communicate density better than thin bars. Consider as future enhancement.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
------------------------
- Slim mode renders 1000-span trace with initial paint < 400ms on a mid-tier laptop (measured local).
- Keyboard navigation (j/k, Enter, f) moves focus predictably; focused span details load within 200ms.
- Filters update visible counts and highlight matching spans on the waterfall.
- Sticky rail shows full span JSON via a single click.

Notes to designers / follow-ups
-----------------------------
- Need a quick mock that shows the slim row at 24px height with micro-metadata alignment. I sketched a few variants (attached in figma: link forthcoming).
- Consider a secondary compact label mode for service names (initials + color) to reduce horizontal overflow in narrow panes.

Quick sketches (ASCII)
---------------------
Top: [filter bar]
Mini: [=============|====] <-- small viewport window
List:  Name  | duration | [waterfall canvas]
1) auth.validate  23ms  | =======--------
2) http.proxy     101ms | ===|===|===|==  <-- small ticks indicate collapsed children
3) db.query       12ms  | --               <-- focused -> details in right rail

Final notes
-----------
This doc is intentionally high-level and experimental. Next step: prototype TR-4123 with a canned 400-span trace and iterate on the keyboard model.

Tracking: I'll convert accepted grooming points to JIRA sub-tasks and attach prototype link for an initial design review with SRE on 2026-02-10.
